chunks.title: [Master Express Lesson 4] The Recorded Session on Custom Models is Here~
chunks.content: # [Master Express Lesson 4] Custom Models Recorded Session This document covers detailed instructions and explanations on setting up and editing custom 3D virtual models including size adjustments, posture modifications, file management, texture editing, importing models from external sources like Daz, and handling actions and animations within the software environment. --- ## Model Selection and Basic Setup This section explains the available default 3D models, differences between versions, and basic model selection criteria important for initial configuration. - Four default models are available in the editor window, primarily used for making bags or character prototypes. - Models include two female and two male versions, with distinctions between V1 (version 5.0) and V2 (post version 5.0). - Age ranges are specified for some models: 6 months old, 6-18 months old, and 7-20 years old. - Models do not have an action folder inherently, so they cannot be saved with actions directly. - Additional style elements such as shoes and hair are available for selection alongside the base models. --- ## Adjusting Model Size and Dimensions This section describes how to customize model dimensions including height, circumference, and detailed body measurements using the virtual model editor. - Access the Virtual Model Editor via the main menu under the virtual model options. - Height settings include: - **All Height**: Full body height excluding the heel. - **HPS Height**: Height from the top of the shoulder (HPS point) to the ground. - Units can be set to millimeters (mm), centimeters (cm), or inches. - Input example: For 1.7 meters height, enter 1700 mm. - Circumference measurements include chest, lower chest, waist, upper hip, and lower hip. - Adjusting one measurement automatically recalculates others based on a database of tens of thousands of human body data points, ensuring realistic proportions. - Basic and advanced measurement options are available: - **Basics**: Standard data used by everyone. - **Advanced**: Includes human body specific measurements; also supports Avanon measurement methods for users with Avanon models. - Gray data fields indicate unmodifiable parameters. --- ## Saving and Loading Custom Models Procedures for saving customized models and reloading them for future use. - After modifications, save models via the save button in the upper right corner. - Create new folders and assign names during save. - Models are saved in **AVS** format. - Saved models can be reopened using the open button next to save. - Arrangement boards and points used for clothing placement can also be saved and loaded with **ARR** file format. --- ## Using Arrangement Boards and Points Guidance on how to use arrangement boards and points to position clothing items on models. - Blue points represent arrangement points; green points represent arrangement boards. - To arrange, open a clothing item (e.g., T-shirt) and place it on the arrangement board. - The arrangement board wraps clothing according to its direction. - Clicking on an arrangement board in the menu highlights it for easy identification. - New arrangement boards can be created with the plus button and renamed.

chunks.content: --- ## Using Arrangement Boards and Points Guidance on how to use arrangement boards and points to position clothing items on models. - Blue points represent arrangement points; green points represent arrangement boards. - To arrange, open a clothing item (e.g., T-shirt) and place it on the arrangement board. - The arrangement board wraps clothing according to its direction. - Clicking on an arrangement board in the menu highlights it for easy identification. - New arrangement boards can be created with the plus button and renamed. - Arrangement boards have horizontal (X) and vertical (Y) joints that can be adjusted for precise positioning. - Layouts can be added to keyboards (a metaphor for arrangement control), with adjustable size and direction parameters for virtual model wrapping. --- ## Adjusting Model Posture and Joints Instructions on modifying virtual model postures by manipulating joint points and movement constraints. - Enable selection window to view skeleton points (green dots). - Joint movement modes: - **Edit All**: Moves all joints simultaneously, preserving body shape. - **Edit Selection**: Moves selected joints and directly linked joints without affecting others. - Movement locking prevents unintended joint displacement during pose adjustments. - Rotation of joints can be controlled to ensure natural posing without unintended rotations. - Example: Rotating the arm or hand affects connected joints; locking rotation prevents unwanted transformations. - Practical use case: Creating a walking pose by selecting foot joints and adjusting positions carefully to avoid unnatural shapes. - Positions can be saved in **POS** file format and recalled later for reuse. --- ## Importing and Using Action Files Details on adding motion and animation data to models to enhance realism. - Animation mode allows loading and playing motion files. - Five default action files can be opened and previewed. - Additional motion files can be downloaded from external platforms including Adobe. - Users can register accounts on these platforms to access and download various action files. - Imported action files can be applied to models to animate them accordingly. --- ## Working with Scanned Models and Model Conversion Explains how to convert scanned 3D models into virtual models and align them within the software. - Important file formats include **OBJ** for model data. - Gender can be assigned or changed during conversion (e.g., male to female). - IK (Inverse Kinematics) connectors can be toggled off to facilitate alignment. - Model alignment requires adjusting angles and positions so scanned and virtual models match. - Height and scale adjustments are necessary to harmonize different models. - Joints can be moved to improve compatibility and smooth transitions. - Models can be renamed and saved after conversion. --- ## Texture Editing and Layer Management Instructions on applying and managing textures on virtual models. - Texture layers can be created and managed within the file manager. - Textures may require processing that can be done via external image editing software like Photoshop. - Tutorials for texture editing are available on the official website. - Textures enhance model realism and customization possibilities.

chunks.content: - Joints can be moved to improve compatibility and smooth transitions. - Models can be renamed and saved after conversion. --- ## Texture Editing and Layer Management Instructions on applying and managing textures on virtual models. - Texture layers can be created and managed within the file manager. - Textures may require processing that can be done via external image editing software like Photoshop. - Tutorials for texture editing are available on the official website. - Textures enhance model realism and customization possibilities. --- ## Importing External Models (e.g., Daz Models) Guidelines for importing models from other 3D applications, focusing on Daz models. - External models must be converted to **OBJ** format for compatibility. - Pay attention to unit measurements; Daz models typically use centimeters. - Preprocessing may be required, such as converting units to millimeters. - Imported models can be dragged into the software and used directly. - Users can create or purchase models from external websites and integrate them. - Imported models retain their original appearance but follow the software’s unit and scale conventions. --- ## Model File Formats and Exporting Explanation of supported file formats and exporting procedures. - Models can be saved and exported as **OBJ** or **FBX** formats. - Exporting is done via the File > Export menu. - OBJ is the most commonly used format for virtual models. - Exported files can be used in other compatible software or platforms. --- ## Additional Tools and Features Covers various additional functionalities, user questions, and clarifications. - The 3D zipper currently only supports a single color; separate color editing for zipper and fabric is not available. - Models can be added directly to the file column via the add button in the drawing book window. - The 3D window grid’s intersecting points serve as coordinate references. - DXF file imports support both straight and curved lines; options are available during import for mesh optimization. - The tool supports reflections on silk metal materials. - Basic T-Pose refers to a standard arm position; tutorials are available for detailed explanations. - Techniques for sewing, making shoes, and using folding scissors (8mm thickness and width) are available in previous tutorials. - Modular settings and further customization options will be covered in upcoming courses. --- ## Live Stream and Playback Information - Live stream recordings may experience delays due to internet speed. - Playback will be available after 7 PM on the live stream day. - Upcoming live streams and courses are scheduled; viewers are encouraged to watch recorded sessions if missed. - Community engagement is encouraged through comments and questions. --- # Summary This document provides a comprehensive guide to using the custom model editor, covering model selection, size and posture adjustments, file management, texture editing, importing external models, animation application, and additional features. It serves as a technical reference for users needing detailed instructions to maximize the software's capabilities in creating and manipulating 3D virtual models.
